$comment: An R implementation for M.MMRM, written by this project on 2026-09-19 because upstream 739344c ships the MMRM method and template with no implementation (log.md V4). Same shape as upstream's M.ANCOVA entry in lib/method_implementations/r_implementations.json. Injected into the running app's methodImplementationCatalog at execution time; the pinned submodule is not edited. Uses the mmrm package, which WebR can install, and which is also what the stage 7 reference is fitted with in local R.
callTemplate:
analysis_data <- <dataset>
analysis_data <- analysis_data[!is.na(analysis_data[["<response>"]]) & !is.na(analysis_data[["<covariate>"]]), , drop = FALSE]
# One row per subject and visit: mmrm refuses duplicate time points, where lm took the first.
# Keep the first, which is the engine's own convention (!duplicated on join keys).
analysis_data <- analysis_data[!duplicated(analysis_data[, c("<repeated_subject>", "<repeated_factor>")]), , drop = FALSE]
# A change-from-baseline model has no baseline row: drop any visit at which every subject's
# change is zero, which is the baseline visit by construction (AVAL minus the baseline AVAL).
zero_visits <- names(which(tapply(analysis_data[["<response>"]], analysis_data[["<repeated_factor>"]], function(x) length(x) > 0 && all(x == 0))))
if (length(zero_visits) > 0) analysis_data <- analysis_data[!(analysis_data[["<repeated_factor>"]] %in% zero_visits), , drop = FALSE]
analysis_data[["<repeated_subject>"]] <- factor(analysis_data[["<repeated_subject>"]])
analysis_data[["<repeated_factor>"]] <- factor(analysis_data[["<repeated_factor>"]])
analysis_data[["<fixed_effect>"]] <- factor(analysis_data[["<fixed_effect>"]])
cov_fn <- switch("<covariance_structure>", UN = "us", CS = "cs", AR1 = "ar1", TOEP = "toep", CSH = "csh", ARH1 = "ar1h", "us")
df_meth <- switch("<df_method>", KR = "Kenward-Roger", Satterthwaite = "Satterthwaite", "Satterthwaite")
use_reml <- identical("<estimation_method>", "REML")
alpha_val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric("<alpha>")); if (is.na(alpha_val)) alpha_val <- 0.05
adj <- "<multiplicity_adjustment>"; if (grepl("<", adj, fixed = TRUE) || !nzchar(adj)) adj <- "none"
# mmrm does not accept non-syntactic column names such as the engine's __col_* derived response,
# so the response and covariate are copied to syntactic names before the fit.
analysis_data$cfb_response <- analysis_data[["<response>"]]
analysis_data$cfb_baseline <- analysis_data[["<covariate>"]]
fml <- as.formula(sprintf("cfb_response ~ cfb_baseline + `%s` * `%s` + %s(`%s` | `%s`)", "<fixed_effect>", "<repeated_factor>", cov_fn, "<repeated_factor>", "<repeated_subject>"))
model <- mmrm::mmrm(fml, data = analysis_data, reml = use_reml, method = df_meth)
model_summary <- summary(model)
coef_tab <- as.data.frame(model_summary$coefficients)
anova_result <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(emmeans::joint_tests(model)), error = function(e) data.frame())
lsm <- emmeans::emmeans(model, as.formula(sprintf("~ `%s` | `%s`", "<fixed_effect>", "<repeated_factor>")))
lsm_df <- as.data.frame(summary(lsm, infer = TRUE, level = 1 - alpha_val))
contr <- pairs(lsm, adjust = adj)
contr_df <- as.data.frame(summary(contr, infer = TRUE, level = 1 - alpha_val))
cov_mat <- mmrm::VarCorr(model)
cov_df <- data.frame(term = paste(rownames(cov_mat)[row(cov_mat)][upper.tri(cov_mat, diag = TRUE)], colnames(cov_mat)[col(cov_mat)][upper.tri(cov_mat, diag = TRUE)], sep = ":"), estimate = cov_mat[upper.tri(cov_mat, diag = TRUE)])
documentation: MMRM on change from baseline: fixed effects baseline covariate, treatment, visit and treatment-by-visit; within-subject covariance over visits (structure from the covariance_structure configuration, default unstructured); REML by default; Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom by default. LS means and treatment contrasts are reported at each visit.
notes: Not an upstream artefact. Written for endpoints/04-vitals-cfb-mmrm; see log.md V4 and V5. Rows are made unique per subject and visit (first kept, the engine's convention) and the baseline visit — the level at which every change is zero — is dropped, because mmrm refuses duplicate time points and a change-from-baseline model has no baseline row (V5).
